title: Cold caller (SDR)
tagline: Learn to open cold calls with small business owners and book qualified demos.
you_are: an outbound sales development representative for a B2B software company
setting: Calls are made from a quiet home office or sales floor using a dialer and CRM, targeting owners who have never heard of the product.

scenarios.label: Gatekeeper screen
scenarios.desc: Reach the decision maker past an assistant or voicemail.
scenarios.setup: You dial a local bakery chain. The owner’s assistant answers, polite but busy, and asks who is calling and what it is regarding.
scenarios.objective: Get transferred to the owner or secure a specific callback time.

scenarios.label: First pitch
scenarios.desc: Deliver the opening value proposition to a skeptical owner.
scenarios.setup: The owner of a 12-person marketing agency picks up. They sound rushed and say they are happy with their current tools.
scenarios.skills: Pattern interrupt, pain discovery, demo framing
scenarios.objective: Book a 20-minute discovery call for later this week.
scenarios.moment: Wednesday 2:40 pm, afternoon glare on the monitor

scenarios.label: Price pushback
scenarios.desc: Handle budget objections after a demo when the owner loves the product but balks at cost.
scenarios.setup: You follow up with a plumbing supply owner who attended a demo last week. They say the ROI makes sense but the monthly fee is double their software budget.
scenarios.skills: Value anchoring, creative financing, next-step commitment
scenarios.objective: Secure a signed agreement or a paid pilot start date.
scenarios.moment: Friday 4:55 pm, long shadows across the keyboard

buyers.role: Executive assistant to a retail chain owner
buyers.angle: She blocks anyone who cannot state a clear business reason in ten seconds.

buyers.role: Founder of a digital marketing agency
buyers.angle: He hears three pitches a day and deletes calendar invites that lack a specific outcome.

buyers.role: Owner of a family-run landscaping business
buyers.angle: She views software as a cost center and needs concrete labor-saving proof.
He will sign only if the payback period is under six months and terms are month-to-month.

buyers.role: Solo attorney modernizing a paper-heavy practice
buyers.angle: She demands data-security addendums and a clause letting her export all data free on exit.

objections: We already use something that works fine
I don’t have budget for new software right now
Send me an email and I’ll look at it later
How are you different from the big platforms?
I’m the wrong person, you need my partner
Your pricing page says per user, that adds up fast
We’ve been burned by long contracts before
Call me next quarter when things settle down

rubric.label: Gatekeeper pass
rubric.what: States a crisp business reason and asks for the owner by name without sounding like a telemarketer.

rubric.label: Pattern interrupt
rubric.what: Breaks the owner’s autopilot with a specific, relevant insight in the first fifteen seconds.

rubric.label: Pain discovery
rubric.what: Asks two to three targeted questions that surface a measurable operational problem.

rubric.label: Demo framing
rubric.what: Positions the demo as a working session on their data, not a generic feature tour.

rubric.label: Value anchoring
rubric.what: Ties price to a concrete savings or revenue number the owner already agreed matters.

rubric.label: Compliance honesty
rubric.what: Represents pricing, data handling, and contract terms accurately with no omitted fees or auto-renewal surprises.

pitfalls: Reading a script verbatim instead of listening and adapting.
Promising features the product roadmap does not guarantee.
Skipping the required TCPA and do-not-call list checks before dialing.
line: Cold calling small business owners for a software company
